{{Quote|There is one lesson you've yet to learn. How to become one with the Force!|Cin Drallig to Darth Vader|<ref name="III game">[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' video game]]</ref>}}
'''Cin Drallig''' was a legendary<ref name="Prima">[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref> [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] who served as [[Battlemaster/Legends|Battlemaster]]<ref name="Insider87Order66" /> and head of [[Temple Security Force|security]]<ref name="DatabankCin" /> at the [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] during the waning days of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. He met his end at the hands of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] during [[Operation: Knightfall/Legends|Operation: Knightfall]], during [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]].

==Biography==
===Early years and rise===
[[File:CinDrallig-Prima.jpg|thumb|left|130px|Cin Drallig]]
The [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] Cin Drallig was [[Youngling/Legends|born]] on [[Lavisar/Legends|Lavisar]].<ref name="Insider87Order66" /><ref name="CSWE" /> Like most [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] of [[Great Peace of the Republic|the era]], it can be surmised that Drallig was brought to the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] soon after being discovered to be [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] and sorted into an [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|Initiate]] [[Clan (Jedi)/Legends|clan]] for group instruction in the [[Jedi academy]]. Here, he would have trained until he graduated the academy and was selected by a [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] as a [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]]. Eventually, Drallig passed the [[Jedi Trials/Legends|Jedi Trials]] and was [[Knighting Ceremony/Legends|made]] a [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] by the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|High Council]].

Later on in his career, Drallig began his servitude as a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] [[Jedi instructor|instructor]], in keeping with the Jedi custom of passing on their special knowledge to the next generation<ref name="DatabankCin" />—especially seeing as Drallig possessed true talent as a swordsman.<ref name="III game" /> Over his career, Drallig taught the basics of Forms I through VI to thousands of students, including such stars-to-be as [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]].<ref name="Insider87Order66" /><ref name="ROTSN" /> In [[31 BBY/Legends|31 BBY]], one of Master Drallig's classes on the seven forms of [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]] was recorded on the [[Great Holocron/Legends|Great Holocron]].<ref name="EGF">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>

At some point, Drallig was introduced to the contentious and troublesome Padawan [[Serra Keto]]. Serra's defiant ways had nearly gotten her expelled from the Order on more than one occasion, and her Jedi Masters were exasperated. Envisioning the great Jedi she had the potential to become, Master Drallig took young Serra as his Padawan and helped her find her center. Under Drallig's guidance, Serra's understanding of the Force and her lightsaber skills blossomed, inspiring a strong bond of devotion between student and Master. Though it never entirely disappeared, Keto's rebelliousness eventually subsided,<ref name="Prima" /> and she went on to become Master Drallig's most accomplished apprentice.<ref name="III game" />

After many years of service and attaining the rank of Jedi Master<ref name="DatabankCin" /><ref name="Prima" /><ref name="III game" /> (no earlier than 31 BBY),<ref name="EGF" /> Drallig was elected [[Battlemaster/Legends|Battlemaster]]<ref name="CSWE" /> (or swordmaster),<ref name="CharEnc" /> making him the leading lightsaber combat instructor in the Temple.<ref name="CSWE" /> Though it smacked of disrespect, Drallig earned the unflattering nickname of "the Troll" among the Order.<ref name="Insider87Order66" /><ref name="CSWE" /><ref name="DatabankCin" /><ref name="ROTSN" />

===Clone Wars===
[[File:Jedi_guards_at_rally.png|thumb|left|250px|Drallig guards the Jedi Temple during a rally.]]
During the time of the galaxy-spanning Clone Wars, Drallig was tasked with protecting the Jedi Temple. As head of security there, he spent most of his time in the Temple, patrolling its corridors and pathways. His position also put him in charge of the [[Jedi Temple Guard/Legends|Jedi Temple Guard]] and their assignments.<ref name="DatabankCin" /><ref name="DatabankJTG">{{SWE|groups|jedi-temple-guard|Jedi Temple Guard}}</ref> As the Clone Wars continued to unfold, Drallig grew particularly concerned with the growing hostility towards the Jedi from Republic citizens.<ref name="DatabankJTG" />

Stationed on Coruscant,<ref name="Insider87Order66" /> Drallig made his home deep within the Jedi Temple.<ref name="Prima" /> Despite his diligent watch on security, however, intrusions into the Temple did happen, such as when [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Cad Bane/Legends|Cad Bane]] [[Raid on the Jedi Temple/Legends|stole]] a [[Holocron/Legends|Jedi holocron]] from a restricted vault and got away.<ref name="DatabankCin" /><ref name="TCW:HH">{{TCW|Holocron Heist}}</ref>

Around [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],<ref name="Death Sentence 1">[[Darth Maul — Death Sentence 1|''Darth Maul — Death Sentence'' 1]]</ref> two years into the war, the Jedi Temple hangar was the site of a shocking [[Bombing of the Jedi Temple hangar/Legends|terrorist bombing]] that cost numerous lives, prompting Cin Drallig to keep an especially close watch on the Temple's perimeter.<ref name="DatabankCin" /> A throng of protestors—family and friends of workers killed in the explosion—gathered at the steps of the Temple to criticize the Jedi's involvement in the war. Flanked by two members of the Jedi Temple Guard, Drallig stood before the masses when Anakin Skywalker showed a [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] of a suspect, [[Jackar Bowmani/Legends|Jackar Bowmani]], to the Jedi Master, which was seen by Bowmani's wife [[Letta Turmond/Legends|Letta Turmond]].<ref name="TCW:S">{{TCW|Sabotage (episode)}}</ref> Master Drallig admired young Skywalker's assertiveness in solving the alarming case,<ref name="DatabankCin" /> but was most concerned at how vulnerable the Order had become, and how the image of the Jedi as benevolent protectors had become much too fragile.

In addition to his responsibilities as head of security, Drallig still found the time to teach lightsaber combat, as indeed the ongoing war placed emphasis on Padawans' combat training in favor of other abilities.<ref name="DatabankZett" /> After the [[Death/Legends|death]] of fellow Jedi [[Mierme Unill]], Unill's Padawan, [[Zett Jukassa/Legends|Zett Jukassa]] was informally assigned to Master Drallig, awaiting reassignment.<ref name="DatabankZett" /> Under Drallig's tutelage, Jukassa became capable as a swordsman by the age of 10, in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="Insider87Order66" />

===Order 66===
[[File:Dralligbenewhie.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Drallig instructed Whie Malreaux and Bene in lightsaber use.]]
In 19 BBY, when the [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]] go-ahead was given and Anakin Skywalker&mdash;now the newly christened Darth Vader&mdash;led the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] in a [[Operation: Knightfall/Legends|raid against the Jedi Temple]], Drallig's skills marked him as a priority target for elimination by the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] himself.<ref name="Insider87Order66" /> Though Jedi Masters [[Shaak Ti/Legends|Shaak Ti]] and [[Jurokk]] directed the Temple's defense the night of Order 66,<ref name="ROTSN" /> Drallig nonetheless played a major part that fateful night. He was in the process of giving lightsaber lessons to teenage Padawans [[Bene/Legends|Bene]] and [[Whie Malreaux/Legends|Whie Malreaux]] when the Sith Lord began his murderous rampage.<ref name="CSWEWhie">{{CSWECite|II|282|Malreaux, Whie}}</ref> Deep within the Jedi Temple he prepared for Vader's coming,<ref name="III game" /> directing such Jedi as [[Olana Chion/Legends|Olana Chion]] in the Temple's defense.<ref name="db">{{DB|character|olanachion|Chion, Olana}}</ref>

Engaging the clones alongside Serra Keto, Drallig's efforts proved initially successful, as he managed to penetrate the occupying forces' upper level defenses. As Vader was alerted to this, however, he went on a hunt for his former lightsaber instructor. Entering Drallig's territory, Vader discovered what carnage had been wrought there, with dead clones and the signs of battle being everywhere. Before Drallig could move against the Dark Lord, however, Serra Keto confronted Vader on her own, and was slain.<ref name="III game" />

As Drallig rushed into the room, he witnessed Keto fall to the Sith Lord.<ref name="III game" /> Engaging Vader in the Temple training hall<ref name="Insider87Order66" /><ref name="III game" /><ref name="c:tp">''[[Star Wars Chronicles: The Prequels]]''</ref> along with two of his students, Bene and Whie Malreaux, they were nonetheless unable to defeat the Dark Lord. Vader outclassed both Padawans, choking Bene with one hand while he dueled Drallig with the other.<ref name="CSWEBene" /><ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref><ref name="DatabankBene">{{DB|character|bene|Bene}}</ref>

Drallig himself ultimately proved unable to defeat a raging Sith Lord in combat.<ref name="CSWE" /> After the demise of the Padawans, the Battlemaster went into a short exchange of lightsaber strikes with Vader before he was hacked down from shoulder to torso. He could only look on in shock and fall to the ground, where he shortly died.<ref name="Unseen Queen">''[[Dark Nest II: The Unseen Queen]]''</ref> The incident was recorded by Temple security camera [[TR4-121]].<ref name="Insider87Order66" />

Drallig's body was later found by Grand Master Yoda and Master Obi-Wan Kenobi, who had [[Infiltration of the Jedi Temple/Legends|returned]] to the Temple to reset the [[Jedi beacon/Legends|emergency beacon]] to warn all surviving Jedi to flee into exile. The discovery caused Kenobi great grief, having considered the Battlemaster a friend.<ref name="ROTSN" /> Kenobi and Yoda also watched the security recording of the Battlemaster's fatal last duel.<ref name="ROTS" />

With the Order nearly extinct overnight, the newly emerged [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] needed to cover up the true reasons for the execution of the Republic's peacekeepers. On behest of [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]] compiled official reasons for each Jedi's death. Incident report #890-I, filed by [[Clone Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Appo/Legends|CC-1119]], contained Master Drallig's certificate of death, while Pestage reported to the public that the Battlemaster had been "killed in combat against Imperial agents."<ref name="Insider87Order66" />

===Legacy===
Cin Drallig's legacy was passed down by those Jedi who survived to train others, including Master Kenobi's training of [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope">{{Film|IV}}</ref>

While still adjusting to his life-supporting armor, Darth Vader often reflected upon the actions that had brought him to such a state. One of his clearer memories was that of crossing blades with Master Drallig, his former lightsaber instructor, the night of Order 66.<ref name="DL">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref>

Drallig's recorded knowledge of the seven forms, made in 31 BBY, was found in the Great Holocron by the [[New Jedi Order]], along with another of his recordings on the marks of contact.<ref name="EGF" />

==Personality and traits==
Cin Drallig was an esteemed Jedi Master, possessing both great skill as a swordsman and a calmness of mind and spirit. Described as patient, focused, and directed, and representing the tenets of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] in their purest form, he had given himself over completely to the will of the [[Living Force/Legends|living Force]]. Despite his great reputation as a warrior, his humbleness of character was such that he dedicated his life to training countless Padawans in the art of the lightsaber, leading by example and instilling in his students a sense of the Order's values and beliefs. Where several other Masters had failed, Drallig was also the only one insightful enough to see the great potential of rebellious Padawan Serra Keto, and reach through to her to make that potential become reality.<ref name="Prima" />

In his recording on the Great Holocron, Drallig presented some personal views on the matter of lightsaber combat. In the wake of death caused by [[Aurra Sing/Legends|Aurra Sing]] and [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], and unlike some Jedi Masters, Cin Drallig refused to dismiss the study of [[Form II/Legends|Form II]] as impractical. He remained cautiously neutral regarding [[Form V/Legends|Form V]], taking the side of neither proponent nor detractor, but emphasizing the need for such an offensive form to be used only with the proper intention of preserving peace. He also conceded that [[Form VI/Legends|Form VI]] being the standard form of the Jedi Order did not mark it as the most worthy of study, but in general the most practical. As for [[Cho mok/Legends|cho mok]], Master Drallig discouraged its use unless the student possessed enough knowledge of the opponent's physiology, so as to not accidentally kill. Master Drallig further stated that a Jedi should not hesitate to use any combat technique to kill a Sith Lord, not even [[Sai tok/Legends|sai tok]]. He stressed that the student's mindset must be that of defeating the danger the Sith pose, not to wish utter destruction upon them.<ref name="EGF" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|Who taught you to fight like this? Was it Cin Drallig? He died like a squealing Gosfamling.|Darth Vader, while luring captured [[Agricultural Corps/Legends|Agricultural Corps]] members to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]]|<ref name="Evasive Action: Recruitment">''[[Evasive Action: Recruitment]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Cin_Drallig_TCW.png|160px|thumb|Cin Drallig was a most capable lightsaber duelist.]]
Cin Drallig's lightsaber instructor was none other than Master Yoda himself,<ref name="CSWE" /><ref name="ROTSN" /> and known for having outstanding talents as a duelist, Drallig became an incredibly skilled swordsman, gaining the rank of Battlemaster of the Order, due to his exceptional prowess in lightsaber combat.<ref name="III game" />

By the time of the Clone Wars, Master Drallig was old<ref name="ROTSN" /> but his age did not hamper his abilities, as he remained one of the Jedi's top swordsmen,<ref name="Insider87Order66" /> his skills described as being "nearly unparalleled."<ref name="Prima" /> Drallig's skill was such that it was the conviction of [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] that the renowned combatant [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] would be no match for the Battlemaster, should they ever face off against one another.<ref name="LOE">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref>

Drallig had developed his own unique style of lightsaber combat, calling upon the Force to enhance his speed and relying on unconventional and unpredictable movements.

Drallig had mastered all seven forms of lightsaber combat and his understanding and knowledge of each form was outstanding enough that he was considered the most prolific lightsaber instructor in the Temple, second only to Yoda himself. He was able to effectively train thousands of students in the use of the Forms I to VI,<ref name="Insider87Order66" /> displaying consummate knowledge of the theory of each form, making thorough comments on each forms strengths and weaknesses. Drallig was also one of the few Jedi to achieve mastery over the Juyo variant of [[Form VII/Legends|Form VII]] but in addition to fully understanding the style's weaknesses and strengths, he was also aware of how dangerous it was due to its aggressiveness and potentially exposing the user to the dark side, hence his caution towards who he would entrust it to. For example, Anakin Skywalker, as a Padawan, lamented the fact that Master Drallig wouldn't let him study Form VII.<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref>

Being the Temple's finest swordmaster at the time of Darth Vader's raid on the Jedi Temple,<ref name="CharEnc" /><ref name="RotSVD">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> Cin Drallig's swordsmanship proved to be great enough to kill off many of the Clones that attacked him and Darth Vader saw the need for he himself to personally fight him. However, for all of his skill, Drallig was no match for the Dark Lord, being cut down in a short exchange as he tried to defend his students. By killing Master Drallig and his apprentice, Serra Keto, Vader had successfully removed one of the Temple's last hopes.<ref name="III game" />

Although his nearly unprecedented mastery of lightsaber combat was his strongest trait, Cin Drallig also proved to be very powerful and accomplished in the use of the Force, displaying high levels of mastery over many Force powers when he fought Vader. He was considerably adept in the use of [[Force speed/Legends|Force speed]], capable of moving fast enough to be invisible to human's eye and often applied it to overwhelm his opponents.<ref name="III game" />

Drallig was also a highly competent leader, being the leader of the security guards of the Jedi Temple during the Clone Wars. Drallig's leadership skills was shown by how he led the remaining Jedi when Operation: Knightfall began to battle the clones, although he was met with defeat.

==Behind the scenes==
In [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], Cin Drallig was played by [[Nick Gillard]], who was the stunt coordinator on all three films of the [[prequel trilogy]]. In the [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (video game)|''Revenge of the Sith'' video game]], the character has Nick Gillard's likeness but is voiced by [[Tom Kane]].

The name "Cin Drallig" comes from [[Tuckerization|reversing Nick Gillard's name]], only removing the "k" in "Nick."

In the novels [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith'']] and ''[[Dark Nest II: The Unseen Queen]]'', Cin Drallig is killed in the [[Room of a Thousand Fountains/Legends|Room of a Thousand Fountains]] (not the Temple training hall), where a large group of younglings were being protected by several Padawans. When Vader arrived in the greenhouse, he cut down Whie Malreaux and another teenage Padawan before quickly overwhelming Drallig and hacking through his shoulder. With Drallig and the older Padawans dead, the remaining children were quickly cut down by [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] fire. When Yoda and Obi-Wan later find Drallig's body, Yoda comments that Drallig would not abandon his young students.<ref name="ROTSN" />

In the film, he is visible only briefly in a holographic recording, but he has a larger role in the video game. In the PS2 version, Cin Drallig managed to knock Vader down, but Vader killed him soon after by impaling him via a [[Telekinesis/Legends|lightsaber throw]], while in the GBA version, Vader triumphed over Drallig. The duel also takes place in the training room above and on the terrace outside the Room of a Thousand Fountains. According to Keeper of the Holocron [[Leland Chee]], Drallig's death as it appears in the game is non-canon. Also, in the film, Drallig has dark blond hair, but in the video game, he has white hair. He is also wearing a different costume.<ref name="III game" /><ref name="SWBoards">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=955#15870004|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Leland Y Chee]]|date=2006-11-01|time=12:47 PM}}</ref>

In the video-game adaptation, Cin appears as character in Duel Mode. When the players both select Cin, one of them controls a seemingly dark-side version of him: dark robes, darker hair and a red lightsaber.<ref name="III game" />

In the [[Star Wars Miniatures]] set ''[[Champions of the Force]]'', the Jedi Weapon Master character resembles Cin Drallig.<ref name="Champions of the Force Preview 3">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/CotFPreview3|text=''Champions of the Force'' Preview 3}}</ref>

For the production of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' [[The Clone Wars: Season Five|fifth-season]] episode "[[Sabotage (episode)|Sabotage]]," a clay maquette of Drallig's head was made by [[Darren Marshall]].<ref name="Sabotage guide">{{SW|url=explore/the-clone-wars/ep517|text="Sabotage" - ''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide|nolive=1}}</ref> In the episode, he was voiced by [[Robin Atkin Downes]].
